  144: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  145: class JobSettings:
  146:     """Everything the user chose. Recorded verbatim in the job record."""
  147: 
  148:     input_path: Path | None
  149:     """The file these coordinates were read from.
  150: 
  151:     **Required, with no default**, the idiom ``longitude_convention`` already
  152:     uses below. ``None`` is a statement, not an absence: "this job came from no
  153:     file". A single typed point says exactly that, and the alternative - a
  154:     fabricated placeholder path - is the plausible default docs/DESIGN.md
  155:     section 1 forbids, because it would put a file name that was never read into
  156:     the job record's INPUT block (amendment #26).
  157: 
  158:     Every read of this field is guarded, and each guard raises its own layer's
  159:     error rather than letting ``None`` travel: ``run`` needs it only when no
  160:     parsed source was handed in, and ``exports.output_stem`` and
  161:     ``report.build_report`` refuse without it.
  162:     """
  163: 
  164:     output_directory: Path | None
  165:     """The folder this job's archive is written into.
  166: 
  167:     **Required, with no default**, and ``None`` is again a statement: "this job
  168:     produces no file". The single-point path converts and displays, writing
  169:     nothing at all, so it has no folder to name and does not invent one.
  170:     ``run`` never reads this field; ``exports.archive_path`` and
  171:     ``report.build_report`` refuse without it (amendment #26).
  172:     """
  173: 
  174:     direction: Direction
  175: 
  176:     source_zone: Zone | None
  177:     target_zone: Zone | None
  178: 
  179:     input_unit: LinearUnit
  180:     output_unit: LinearUnit
  181: 
  182:     longitude_convention: LongitudeConvention | None
  183:     """Which sign convention the file's longitudes use.
  184: 
  185:     **Required, with no default** (docs/DESIGN.md section 7). A default here is
  186:     the failure the rule exists to prevent: a geodetic input file written
  187:     positive west, converted as though it were negative west, lands 11,634,618 m
  188:     away carrying nothing louder than an outside-zone-extent warning. The field
  189:     is declared before the defaulted fields only because a frozen dataclass may
  190:     not put a field without a default after one that has one.
  191: 
  192:     ``None`` is a statement, not an absence: "this job never consults the
  193:     convention". Only a pure zone-to-zone job may say it - the grid coordinates
  194:     on both ends carry no longitude - and ``run`` refuses any other direction
  195:     that arrives with None rather than choosing one.
  196:     """
  197: 
  198:     geoid_model: geoid.GeoidModel | None = geoid.GEOID18_MODEL
  199:     """The geoid model whose separations this job's factors are computed from.
  200: 
  201:     Replaces ``apply_geoid: bool`` (WP-V5, docs/PLAN-vertical-datums.md section
  202:     3.5): a bool could say only that *some* geoid was applied, and the job
  203:     record then named the model from a module constant that a second model
  204:     made ambiguous. The record chosen here is the one the audit CSV and the
  205:     job record report, so the settings and the outputs cannot disagree about
  206:     which grid the factors came from.
  207: 
  208:     ``None`` is a statement, not an absence - "no geoid was applied to this
  209:     job" - the idiom ``input_path`` and ``output_directory`` already use. No
  210:     interface offers it (the owner's "no none", plan section 5); it is a
  211:     capability of the core, kept so report.py's "Geoid model not applied"
  212:     branch stays honest and tested rather than dead.
  213:     """
  214: 
  215:     geodetic_frame: ReferenceFrame = NAD83_2011
  216:     """The reference frame this job's GEODETIC end is expressed in.
  217: 
  218:     Read at both geodetic ends, not only the input one: on
  219:     ``GEODETIC_TO_ZONE`` it is the frame the file's latitudes and longitudes
  220:     are read as, and on ``ZONE_TO_GEODETIC`` it is the frame the latitudes and
  221:     longitudes written out are in - which is the source zone's frame, not a
  222:     choice. Unread by ``ZONE_TO_ZONE``, where both ends are zones carrying
  223:     their own.
  224: 
  225:     **NATRF2022 is now a legitimate value** (docs/DESIGN.md amendment #62). It
  226:     was not when this field was written: NATRF2022 had no zones and setting
  227:     this field to it was, in the words this docstring used to carry, the only
  228:     way to reach a mismatch on purpose. Nineteen Michigan SPCS2022 zones are
  229:     defined on it now, and a geodetic job against one of them states NATRF2022
  230:     here and converts. What refuses is the pair, not the frame: the
  231:     NAD83(2011) <-> NATRF2022 bridge is deferred with NGS's own transformation
  232:     unpublished (docs/DEFERRED-NATRF2022-BRIDGE.md), so a frame that disagrees
  233:     with the zone at the other end is refused by
  234:     ``_require_a_registered_frame_path`` before the file is read, and by
  235:     ``convert.require_frame_path`` again at every point.
  236: 
  237:     **The default is now load-bearing in a way it was not**, and this is worth
  238:     stating rather than discovering: it is NAD83(2011), which is right for
  239:     every SPCS 83 job and WRONG for every 2022-zone geodetic job. Wrong here
  240:     means refused, never converted - the gate above - so the cost of the
  241:     default is a refusal a caller must answer, not a coordinate. It stays a
  242:     default because changing it would silently move every existing caller's
  243:     job, and because the frame is still not the coin-flip the longitude sign
  244:     is: the manual uses one longitude convention and every GPS and GIS the
  245:     other, the two are indistinguishable from the numbers, and choosing wrongly
  246:     throws a Michigan point about 340 miles, which is why docs/DESIGN.md
  247:     section 7 forbids a default THERE.
  248: 
  249:     It is a field on the settings rather than a constant inside the loop
  250:     precisely so it is visible: the job record states the frame the input was
  251:     interpreted as, because a record that does not say which frame it assumed is
  252:     not a record.
  253:     """
  254: 
  255:     vertical_mode: VerticalMode = VerticalMode.HORIZONTAL
  256:     """Whether elevations are converted between vertical datums.
  257: 
  258:     Defaults to ``HORIZONTAL`` because that default preserves every existing
  259:     caller's behaviour exactly - it is today's job, and it asserts nothing
  260:     about a vertical datum. The GUI toggle that offers the other mode is
 1640:     """The datum tag is CHECKED, not carried (DESIGN.md #36 reviewer note).
 1641: 
 1642:     ``apply_shift`` takes a bare float, so nothing downstream could notice a
 1643:     transformation looked up for one pair of datums being applied to a job
 1644:     that stated another - the shifted height would look entirely ordinary.
 1645:     ``run`` passes down the record ``require_vertical_pair`` returned for the
 1646:     settings' own datums; this holds that wiring at the point of use, by
 1647:     ``code``, the rule the registry itself resolves by. if/raise, never
 1648:     assert: the suite and the shipped program run under -O.
 1649:     """
 1650:     stated_source = settings.source_vertical_datum
 1651:     stated_target = settings.target_vertical_datum
 1652:     source_code = stated_source.code if stated_source is not None else None
 1653:     target_code = stated_target.code if stated_target is not None else None
 1654:     if (
 1655:         transformation.source.code != source_code
 1656:         or transformation.target.code != target_code
 1657:     ):
 1658:         raise ValueError(
 1659:             f"The vertical transformation applied to this row converts "
 1660:             f"{transformation.source.code} -> {transformation.target.code}, "
 1661:             f"but the job's settings state {source_code} -> {target_code}. "
 1662:             f"Applying it would move every elevation between datums nobody "
 1663:             f"chose, and nothing downstream could tell: the shift is a bare "
 1664:             f"number and the shifted height looks ordinary. The record must "
 1665:             f"be the one require_vertical_pair returned for the settings' "
 1666:             f"own datums."
 1667:         )
 1668: 
 1669: 
 1670: def _require_geodetic_in_range(
 1671:     latitude: float,
 1672:     longitude: float,
 1673:     longitude_as_written: float,
 1674:     settings: JobSettings,
 1675:     context: str,
 1676: ) -> None:
 1677:     """Refuse a latitude or longitude no signed geodetic position can carry.
 1678: 
 1679:     Placed here - the single entry point where the file's longitude sign
 1680:     convention is applied - rather than left to the core, so the refusal can
 1681:     name the row, the value as the file wrote it, and the convention in
 1682:     force, none of which ``lambert._require_valid_geodetic`` (which guards
 1683:     the same domain and still runs after this) can see.
 1684: 
 1685:     Recorded against DESIGN.md #38's note to WP-V6: the NGS grid readers
 1686:     accept 0-360 east longitudes silently - ``to_east_longitude`` adjusts
 1687:     only negatives, so ``shift_m(43.0, 275.5)`` equals
 1688:     ``shift_m(43.0, -84.5)`` byte-identically. Through ``job.run`` the
 1689:     horizontal conversion's own domain gate already refused such a value
 1690:     before any grid was consulted; this refusal keeps that property stated
 1691:     at the boundary that owns it instead of inherited from the projection's
 1692:     internals, and says which ROW is wrong, which a file of thousands of
 1693:     points needs.
 1694: 
 1695:     The bounds are the core's exactly - latitude strictly inside (-90, 90),
 1696:     longitude within [-180, 180] - so no value can pass here and refuse
 1697:     there, or the reverse. NaN fails both comparisons and is refused too.
 1698:     """
 1699:     convention = settings.longitude_convention.value
 1700:     if not (-90.0 < latitude < 90.0):
 1701:         raise ValueError(
 1702:             f"{context}: the latitude column reads {latitude!r}, which is "
 1703:             f"not a geodetic latitude - it must lie strictly between -90 and "
 1704:             f"90 degrees. Check that the file's second column really holds "
 1705:             f"latitudes in decimal degrees, and that the latitude and "
 1706:             f"longitude columns are not swapped. Refused rather than "
 1707:             f"converted, because a coordinate computed from it would look "
 1708:             f"ordinary and be meaningless."
 1709:         )
 1710:     if not (-180.0 <= longitude <= 180.0):
 1711:         advice = (
 1712:             f"Subtract 360 from it ({longitude - 360.0:.6f} here), or export "
 1713:             f"the file again with signed longitudes."
 1714:             if 180.0 < longitude < 360.0
 1715:             else "Correct the file, or the convention selected for it."
 1716:         )
 1717:         raise ValueError(
 1718:             f"{context}: the longitude column reads {longitude_as_written!r}, "
 1719:             f"which under the '{convention}' convention this job states is a "
 1720:             f"signed longitude of {longitude!r} - outside the -180 to 180 "
 1721:             f"range a signed longitude can have. A value between 180 and 360 "
 1722:             f"is the 0-360 EAST convention, which this program deliberately "
 1723:             f"does not read from a file: 275.5 east and -84.5 both name the "
 1724:             f"same meridian, and the NGS grid files use 0-360 internally, so "
 1725:             f"an unconverted 0-360 longitude would look up plausible geoid "
 1726:             f"and VERTCON values while the State Plane conversion placed the "
 1727:             f"point thousands of kilometres away. " + advice
 1728:         )
 1729: 
 1730: 
 1731: def per_side_geoid_models(
 1732:     settings: JobSettings, transformation: VerticalTransformation | None
 1733: ) -> tuple[geoid.GeoidModel | None, geoid.GeoidModel | None]:
 1734:     """``(input-side model, output-side model)`` for this job, normalized.
 1735: 
 1736:     THE one statement of the per-side pairing (the owner's feature,
 1737:     2026-08-09), read by the computation, the factors rule, the swap
 1738:     detection and the record, so no two of them can pair differently.
 1739: 
 1740:     The normalization SUPERSEDES DESIGN.md #41's either-endpoint contortion
 1741:     by generalization: each side's model must match its own side's datum.
 1742:     The one pre-existing call shape that put a source-era model in
 1743:     ``geoid_model`` - a modeled transformation whose SOURCE datum is the
 1744:     model's era but whose target is not (NAVD88 -> NGVD29 with GEOID18, the
 1745:     configuration #41 widened the rule for) - is treated as the input-side
 1746:     model here, so every #41-era caller keeps working, its factors and
 1747:     outputs bit-identical, and ``factors_use_source_era`` becomes a
 1748:     consequence of the pairing rather than a parallel rule.
 1749:     """
 1750:     source_model = settings.source_geoid_model
 1751:     output_model = settings.geoid_model
 1752:     if (
 1753:         transformation is not None
 1754:         and not transformation.is_identity
 1755:         and output_model is not None
 1756:         and source_model is None
 1757:         and output_model.vertical_datum.code == transformation.source.code
 1758:         and output_model.vertical_datum.code != transformation.target.code
 1759:     ):
 1760:         return output_model, None
 1761:     return source_model, output_model
 1762: 
 1763: 
 1764: def factors_geoid_model(
 1765:     settings: JobSettings, transformation: VerticalTransformation | None
 1766: ) -> geoid.GeoidModel | None:
 1767:     """The model this job's factors are computed from, or None.
 1768: 
 1769:     The side whose height and separation share an era: the OUTPUT side where
 1770:     it has a model - the factors then describe the height the Z column
 1771:     carries - else the INPUT side, else no model at all (the factors read
 1772:     N/A). One statement, shared by ``run``, the record and the audit CSV's
 1773:     "Geoid model" column, so they cannot name different grids.
 1774:     """
 1775:     source_model, output_model = per_side_geoid_models(settings, transformation)
 1776:     return output_model if output_model is not None else source_model
 1777: 
 1778: 
 1779: def geoid_swap_models(
 1780:     settings: JobSettings, transformation: VerticalTransformation | None
 1781: ) -> tuple[geoid.GeoidModel, geoid.GeoidModel] | None:
 1782:     """``(input model, output model)`` when this job converts BETWEEN geoid
 1783:     models, else None.
 1784: 
 1785:     A geoid-to-geoid conversion is exactly: an identity vertical
 1786:     transformation (the datum does not change) with a model stated on each
 1787:     side and the two models different. The same model on both sides is the
 1788:     ordinary identity job - no swap step, no record - and a modeled
 1789:     transformation with both sides stated was refused before any point
 1790:     converted (``run``'s compound-job refusal).
 1791:     """
 1792:     if transformation is None or not transformation.is_identity:
 1793:         return None
 1794:     source_model, output_model = per_side_geoid_models(settings, transformation)
 1795:     if source_model is None or output_model is None:
 1796:         return None
 1797:     if source_model == output_model:
 1798:         return None
 1799:     return source_model, output_model
 1800: 
 1801: 
 1802: def factors_use_source_era(
 1803:     settings: JobSettings, transformation: VerticalTransformation | None
 1804: ) -> bool:
 1805:     """Whether this job's factors are computed from the SOURCE-datum height.
 1806: 
 1807:     The #41 either-endpoint rule's one configuration where the factors do not
 1808:     use the height the Z column carries - now a CONSEQUENCE of the per-side
 1809:     pairing (``per_side_geoid_models``): the factors follow the one side
 1810:     that has a model, and on a modeled transformation only the input side
 1811:     can honestly hold one whose era is the source datum's. Stated once and
 1812:     called from both the computation (``_convert_row``) and the record
 1813:     (``report.py``'s Factor height paragraph), so the sentence and the
 1814:     arithmetic cannot drift apart (WP-V7 review gate, LOW 2; one
 1815:     authoritative representation per fact).
 1816:     """
 1817:     if transformation is None or transformation.is_identity:
 1818:         return False
 1819:     source_model, output_model = per_side_geoid_models(settings, transformation)
 1820:     return output_model is None and source_model is not None

  283:     source_geoid_model: geoid.GeoidModel | None = None
  284:     """The geoid model the INPUT elevations are stated against, or None.
  285: 
  286:     The owner's per-side feature (2026-08-09): on a vertical job the input
  287:     and output geoid models are chosen separately, so ``geoid_model`` above
  288:     is the OUTPUT side and this field is the INPUT side. ``None`` is a
  289:     statement, not an absence - "no input-side geoid model is stated" -
  290:     which is every job this program ran before the field existed.
  291: 
  292:     The rules ``run`` enforces, in the order it enforces them:
  293: 
  294:     * a HORIZONTAL job refuses this field outright: no vertical question was
  295:       asked, so an input-side geoid model answers nothing;
  296:     * each side's model must match its own side's vertical datum (the
  297:       per-side form of DESIGN.md #32's two-eras rule);
  298:     * BOTH sides carrying a model on a NON-identity transformation refuses:
  299:       that job would compound a modeled datum shift with a modeled geoid
  300:       change inside one Z column, and the honest form is two jobs;
  301:     * both sides carrying DIFFERENT models on an IDENTITY transformation is
  302:       the geoid-to-geoid conversion: the ellipsoid height is held fixed and
  303:       the orthometric height re-derived under the output model,
  304:       ``H_out = H_in + N_in - N_out`` (``GeoidSwapReading``). The same model
  305:       on both sides is exactly the identity job this program always ran -
  306:       no swap step, no new record.
  307: 
  308:     Compatibility (superseding DESIGN.md #41's either-endpoint contortion by
  309:     GENERALIZATION): a pre-existing call shape that put a SOURCE-era model in
  310:     ``geoid_model`` on a modeled job - NAVD88 -> NGVD29 with GEOID18, the one
  311:     configuration #41 existed for - is normalized to this field internally
  312:     (``per_side_geoid_models``), so every #41-era call keeps working and the
  313:     old ``factors_use_source_era`` outcome falls out of per-side pairing
  314:     rather than a special rule.
  315:     """
  316: 
  317:     input_height_kind: HeightKind = HeightKind.ORTHOMETRIC
  318:     """What the input Z column HOLDS - an elevation, or a GNSS height.
  319: 
  320:     ORTHOMETRIC by default, and the default is load-bearing: it is what every
  321:     survey file this program has read contained and what it assumed silently
  322:     before this field existed, so every pre-existing job is unchanged to the
  323:     byte. This is one of the few defaults in the program, and it earns its
  324:     place the way ``VerticalMode.HORIZONTAL`` does - the default member IS the
  325:     status quo, so nothing is assumed that was not already being assumed.
  326: 
  327:     ELLIPSOID says the Z column holds heights above the GRS 80 ellipsoid, as a
  328:     GNSS receiver produces them. The program then computes H = h - N at each
  329:     point from the job's geoid model, and what it DOES with H depends on the
  330:     mode - the only place in this feature where the mode matters:
  331: 
  332:     * **HORIZONTAL**: the Z column is written back exactly as supplied (the
  333:       owner's instruction, 2026-08-11) and only the FACTORS change. That is
  334:       not cosmetic: the elevation factor is R / (R + H + N), so a height that
  335:       already contains the separation gets it added twice, which in Michigan
  336:       is ~34 m of denominator - about **5 ppm** on every combined factor, a
  337:       third of a foot in ten miles, always the same direction.
  338:     * **HORIZONTAL_AND_VERTICAL and VERTICAL**: H is the height, and it goes
  339:       on to the datum shift and into the Z column, datum-tagged.
  340: 
  341:     The rules ``run`` enforces:
  342: 
  343:     * ELLIPSOID with no geoid model on either side refuses - there is no N,
  344:       so there is no H;
  345:     * ELLIPSOID on a vertical job whose ``source_vertical_datum`` is not the
  346:       model's own datum refuses: an ellipsoid height is in no vertical datum,
  347:       and the H derived from it is in the MODEL's, so any other input datum
  348:       would mislabel it before a single shift ran;
  349:     * ELLIPSOID on a geoid-to-geoid job refuses. The input model cancels out
  350:       of ``(h - N_in) + (N_in - N_out)``, so the input selection changes no
  351:       number - and the record would state a conversion "from GEOID12B" of a
  352:       height that was never on GEOID12B, a false sentence in an audit
  353:       document (the owner's decision, 2026-08-11).
  354:     """
  355: 
  356: 
  357: _IDENTITY_SIGMA_REASON = (
  358:     "no modeled transformation was applied, so no model uncertainty exists"
  359: )
  360: """Why an identity reading carries no sigma. NOT sigma 0.0: a zero would state
  361: that the conversion's uncertainty was measured and found to be nothing, when in
  362: truth no model ran and there is no model uncertainty to state - fabricating a
  363: zero uncertainty is the same class of invented number as fabricating a zero
  364: shift, and this program refuses both."""

 1020:     if settings.source_geoid_model is not None and not isinstance(
 1021:         settings.source_geoid_model, geoid.GeoidModel
 1022:     ):
 1023:         # The impostor guard ``geoid_model`` carries above, for the input

 1025:         # habits reach both. if/raise, never assert (-O strips asserts).

 1028:             f"GeoidModel record, or None to state that no input-side geoid "
 1029:             f"model is stated; got "
 1030:             f"{type(settings.source_geoid_model).__name__} "
 1031:             f"({settings.source_geoid_model!r}). Pass geoid.GEOID18_MODEL, "
 1032:             f"geoid.GEOID12B_MODEL, or a record from "
 1033:             f"geoid.geoid_model_by_name()."
 1034:         )
 1035: 
 1036:     if (
 1037:         settings.source_geoid_model is not None
 1038:         and settings.source_geoid_model not in geoid.ALL_GEOID_MODELS
 1039:     ):
 1040:         # Registry membership, the geoid_model rule above verbatim: the job
 1041:         # record cites the input model's tile and digest from the registry,
 1042:         # so a model the registry does not hold cannot be documented.
 1043:         known = ", ".join(model.name for model in geoid.ALL_GEOID_MODELS)
 1044:         raise ValueError(
 1045:             f"JobSettings.source_geoid_model "
 1046:             f"{settings.source_geoid_model.name!r} is not a registered geoid "
 1047:             f"model, so the job record could not cite its tile and checksum. "
 1048:             f"A job converts only against the models this program ships: "
 1049:             f"{known}. Use the records in michspc.fileio.geoid, or "
 1050:             f"geoid_model_by_name()."
 1051:         )
 1052: 
 1053:     if transformation is None and settings.source_geoid_model is not None:
 1054:         # A horizontal job asked no vertical question, so an input-side
 1055:         # geoid model answers nothing - the mirror of the vertical-datum
 1056:         # refusal, arriving at the new field. Silently ignoring it would let
 1057:         # a caller believe the input elevations' geoid statement was used.
 1058:         raise ValueError(
 1059:             f"This job is horizontal-only, but source_geoid_model "
 1060:             f"({settings.source_geoid_model.name}) was supplied. An "
 1061:             f"input-side geoid model exists to convert elevations between "
 1062:             f"geoid models, and a horizontal job converts no elevation at "
 1063:             f"all. Set vertical_mode to a mode that converts elevations, or "
 1064:             f"state None; a horizontal job's factors come from geoid_model "
 1065:             f"alone."
 1066:         )
 1067: 
 1068:     if (
 1069:         transformation is not None
 1070:         and not transformation.is_identity
 1071:         and settings.geoid_model is not None
 1072:         and settings.source_geoid_model is not None
 1073:     ):
 1074:         # The compound-job refusal: a modeled datum shift AND a geoid change
 1075:         # inside one Z column would stack two modeled corrections with no
 1076:         # surface stating either alone. The honest form is two jobs, each
 1077:         # with its own record - and the refusal says so rather than picking
 1078:         # an order of application nobody stated. Guarded before the
 1079:         # per-side era checks below, because the advice here (split the job)
 1080:         # is the one that survives whichever era pairing arrives with it -
 1081:         # today only NAVD 88 has published models, so this fires ahead of a
 1082:         # NAPGD2022-era registry rather than after it.
 1083:         raise ValueError(
 1084:             f"This job states a geoid model on BOTH sides "
 1085:             f"(source_geoid_model={settings.source_geoid_model.name}, "
 1086:             f"geoid_model={settings.geoid_model.name}) of a modeled vertical "
 1087:             f"transformation ({transformation.source.code} -> "
 1088:             f"{transformation.target.code}). That would compound a modeled "
 1089:             f"datum shift with a modeled geoid change inside one elevation, "
 1090:             f"and no output could say which correction moved the height. "
 1091:             f"Run two jobs: convert between the geoid models in an identity "
 1092:             f"job ({transformation.source.code} -> "
 1093:             f"{transformation.source.code}), then convert the datum with "
 1094:             f"one geoid model stated."
 1095:         )
 1096: 
 1097:     if transformation is not None and settings.source_geoid_model is not None:
 1098:         # The per-side form of DESIGN.md #32's two-eras rule: the INPUT
 1099:         # model's separations must be published for the INPUT elevations'
 1100:         # own datum, because H_in + N_in is the ellipsoid height only when
 1101:         # the two share an era. The output side keeps the guard below.
 1102:         model = settings.source_geoid_model
 1103:         if model.vertical_datum.code != settings.source_vertical_datum.code:
 1104:             raise geoid.GeoidError(
 1105:                 f"The {model.name} geoid model publishes separations for "
 1106:                 f"heights in {model.vertical_datum.code}, and this job's "
 1107:                 f"INPUT elevations are "
 1108:                 f"{settings.source_vertical_datum.code}, so there is no "
 1109:                 f"input height its separations can honestly combine with - "
 1110:                 f"an ellipsoid height built from the two would mix eras "
 1111:                 f"inside one number (DESIGN.md #32). State an input-side "
 1112:                 f"model published for "
 1113:                 f"{settings.source_vertical_datum.code} heights, or none."
 1114:             )
 1115: 
 1116:     if transformation is not None and settings.geoid_model is not None:
 1117:         # Plan section 3.5's fourth refusal, WIDENED at the WP-V6 review gate
 1118:         # (DESIGN.md #41, superseding the plan's target-datum-only rule): the
 1119:         # geoid model's datum must match EITHER endpoint of the vertical
 1120:         # conversion, because the factors are computed from the height in the
 1121:         # model's own era - the shifted height when the target matches, the
 1122:         # source height when the source does (_convert_row). The plan's rule
 1123:         # would have refused NAVD88 -> NGVD29 outright, dead-ending WP-V8's
 1124:         # dropdowns for every NGVD 29 target with advice no interface offers;
 1125:         # under this rule both modeled directions carry a NAVD 88 leg and
 1126:         # work with both shipped models, and the era mixing #32 forbids never
 1127:         # happens. What still refuses: a pair whose endpoints BOTH differ
 1128:         # from the model's datum - today, only an NGVD29 -> NGVD29 identity
 1129:         # job with a geoid model attached, where no NAVD 88 height exists at
 1130:         # any stage. After the job's own geoid_model guards above, so a geoid
 1131:         # impostor is still refused by the job's own message first.
 1132:         model = settings.geoid_model
 1133:         endpoint_codes = {
 1134:             settings.source_vertical_datum.code,
 1135:             settings.target_vertical_datum.code,
 1136:         }
 1137:         if model.vertical_datum.code not in endpoint_codes:
 1138:             raise geoid.GeoidError(
 1139:                 f"The {model.name} geoid model publishes separations for "
 1140:                 f"heights in {model.vertical_datum.code}, but no stage of "
 1141:                 f"this job's elevations is in that datum "
 1142:                 f"({settings.source_vertical_datum.code} -> "
 1143:                 f"{settings.target_vertical_datum.code}), so there is no "
 1144:                 f"height the model's separations can honestly combine with - "
 1145:                 f"an elevation factor built from the two would mix eras "
 1146:                 f"inside one number (DESIGN.md #32). Run this job in "
 1147:                 f"horizontal mode, which converts the coordinates and "
 1148:                 f"carries the elevation through unchanged, or convert the "
 1149:                 f"elevations to {model.vertical_datum.code} in a job that "
 1150:                 f"targets it."
 1151:             )
 1152: 
 1153:     # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 1154:     # Ellipsoid input's refusals, all before any point converts (the owner's
 1155:     # feature, 2026-08-11). They sit here, after the geoid-model guards
 1156:     # above, so a model impostor is still refused by its own message first
 1157:     # and these never fire on a nonsense record.
 1158:     # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 1159:     if not isinstance(settings.input_height_kind, HeightKind):
 1160:         raise TypeError(
 1161:             f"JobSettings.input_height_kind must be a HeightKind stating what "
 1162:             f"the Z column holds; got "
 1163:             f"{type(settings.input_height_kind).__name__} "
 1164:             f"({settings.input_height_kind!r}). In particular True is not "
 1165:             f"'the ellipsoid one'."
 1166:         )
 1167: 
 1168:     if settings.input_height_kind is HeightKind.ELLIPSOID:
 1169:         ellipsoid_model = factors_geoid_model(settings, transformation)
 1170:         if ellipsoid_model is None:
 1171:             raise geoid.GeoidError(
 1172:                 "This job states that its input heights are ELLIPSOID "
 1173:                 "heights, but it carries no geoid model on either side. An "
 1174:                 "ellipsoid height is measured from the GRS 80 ellipsoid; "
 1175:                 "turning it into an elevation needs the geoid separation N at "
 1176:                 "each point, and with no model there is none - so there is no "
 1177:                 "orthometric height to compute, to write, or to build a "
 1178:                 "factor from. Choose a geoid model, or state that the Z "
 1179:                 "column holds orthometric heights."
 1180:             )
 1181: 
 1182:         if geoid_swap_models(settings, transformation) is not None:
 1183:             raise geoid.GeoidError(
 1184:                 f"This job states ELLIPSOID input heights AND a geoid change "
 1185:                 f"({settings.source_geoid_model.name} -> "
 1186:                 f"{settings.geoid_model.name}). Those two cannot be combined, "
 1187:                 f"and not because the arithmetic fails - because it makes the "
 1188:                 f"input model meaningless. An ellipsoid height is on no geoid "
 1189:                 f"model at all, so (h - N_in) + (N_in - N_out) is just "
 1190:                 f"h - N_out: the input model cancels out and changes no "
 1191:                 f"number this job produces, while every output would state a "
 1192:                 f"conversion FROM {settings.source_geoid_model.name} of a "
 1193:                 f"height that was never on it. State "
 1194:                 f"{settings.geoid_model.name} on both sides to get "
 1195:                 f"orthometric heights on {settings.geoid_model.name}."
 1196:             )
 1197: 
 1198:         if transformation is not None:
 1199:             source_code = settings.source_vertical_datum.code
 1200:             if ellipsoid_model.vertical_datum.code != source_code:
 1201:                 raise geoid.GeoidError(
 1202:                     f"This job states ELLIPSOID input heights and an INPUT "
 1203:                     f"vertical datum of {source_code}. An ellipsoid height is "
 1204:                     f"measured from the GRS 80 ellipsoid and is in no "
 1205:                     f"vertical datum at all; the orthometric height this "

 1208:                     f"{ellipsoid_model.vertical_datum.code} for "

 1217:                 )

 1220:     # The factors' grid: the one side whose height and separation share an
 1221:     # era (factors_geoid_model - output side preferred, else input side).
 1222:     # For every pre-existing call shape this is settings.geoid_model's own
 1223:     # grid, bit for bit: the #41-era NAVD88 -> NGVD29 shape normalizes its

 1225:     factors_model = factors_geoid_model(settings, transformation)
 1226:     grid = (
 1227:         geoid.default_grid(factors_model) if factors_model is not None else None
 1228:     )
 1229: 
 1230:     # The geoid-to-geoid conversion's two grids, loaded once per job exactly
 1231:     # as the factors grid above is. None on every job that is not a swap -
 1232:     # including the same model stated on both sides, which is the ordinary
 1233:     # identity job with no swap step.
 1234:     swap_models = geoid_swap_models(settings, transformation)
 1235:     swap_grids = (
 1823: def _convert_row(
 1824:     row: pnezd.PnezdRow,
 1825:     settings: JobSettings,
 1826:     grid,
 1827:     transformation: VerticalTransformation | None,
 1828:     vertcon_grids: vertcon.VertconGridPair | None,
 1829:     swap_grids: _GeoidSwapGrids | None = None,
 1830: ) -> ConvertedPoint:
 1831:     context = f"point {row.point_id}"
 1832:     warnings: list[ConversionWarning] = []
 1833: 
 1834:     geodetic_input = settings.direction is Direction.GEODETIC_TO_ZONE or (
 1835:         settings.direction is Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY
 1836:         and settings.source_zone is None
 1837:     )
 1838: 
 1839:     if geodetic_input:
 1840:         # The file's "northing" and "easting" columns hold latitude and
 1841:         # longitude. The longitude is normalised to the program's signed
 1842:         # convention here, at the boundary, and nowhere else.
 1843:         latitude = row.northing
 1844:         longitude = settings.longitude_convention.to_signed(row.easting)
 1845:         _require_geodetic_in_range(
 1846:             latitude, longitude, row.easting, settings, context
 1847:         )
 1848:         if settings.direction is Direction.GEODETIC_TO_ZONE:
 1849:             conversion = project_point(
 1850:                 latitude,
 1851:                 longitude,
 1852:                 settings.geodetic_frame,
 1853:                 settings.target_zone,
 1854:                 context,
 1855:             )
 1856:             output_unit = settings.output_unit
 1857:             output_northing = output_unit.from_meters(conversion.target_northing)
 1858:             output_easting = output_unit.from_meters(conversion.target_easting)
 1859:         else:
 1860:             # VERTICAL_ONLY, geodetic input. No zone exists anywhere in this
 1861:             # job, and none is fabricated: the position record carries the
 1862:             # pivot for the grid lookups and None for every zone-derived
 1863:             # quantity, so the grid scale and combined factors downstream are
 1864:             # honestly absent rather than invented. The output coordinate
 1865:             # columns are the INPUT values, unchanged - the mirror this
 1866:             # direction promises - including the longitude exactly as the
 1867:             # file wrote it, in its own convention.
 1868:             conversion = geodetic_position(
 1869:                 latitude, longitude, settings.geodetic_frame, context
 1870:             )
 1871:             output_northing = row.northing
 1872:             output_easting = row.easting
 1873:     else:
 1874:         northing_m = settings.input_unit.to_meters(row.northing)
 1875:         easting_m = settings.input_unit.to_meters(row.easting)
 1876: 
 1877:         if easting_looks_wrong_for_zone(easting_m, settings.source_zone):
 1878:             warnings.append(
 1879:                 ConversionWarning(
 1880:                     code=WarningCode.EASTING_UNLIKE_SELECTED_ZONE,
 1881:                     message=(
 1882:                         f"{context}: an easting of {row.easting:,.3f} "
 1883:                         f"{settings.input_unit.code} does not look like "
 1884:                         f"{settings.source_zone.name} data, whose eastings sit "
 1885:                         f"near {settings.input_unit.from_meters(settings.source_zone.definition.easting_origin):,.0f} "
 1886:                         # "this file" was wrong the moment a typed point could
 1887:                         # raise this warning: the single-point tab has no file,
 1888:                         # and this is the likeliest warning a typed point
 1889:                         # produces. Worded for both callers (closing review
 1890:                         # gate, docs/DESIGN.md amendment #26).
 1891:                         f"{settings.input_unit.code}. Check that the source "
 1892:                         f"zone and the input units are the ones these "
 1893:                         f"coordinates are actually in - selecting the wrong "
 1894:                         f"source zone is the easiest mistake to make with this "
 1895:                         f"program."
 1896:                     ),
 1897:                 )
 1898:             )
 1899: 
 1900:         if settings.direction is Direction.ZONE_TO_GEODETIC:
 1901:             conversion = convert_point(
 1902:                 northing_m,
 1903:                 easting_m,
 1904:                 settings.source_zone,
 1905:                 settings.source_zone,
 1906:                 context,
 1907:             )
 1908:             output_northing = conversion.latitude
 1909:             output_easting = settings.longitude_convention.from_signed(
 1910:                 conversion.longitude
 1911:             )
 1912:         elif settings.direction is Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY:
 1913:             # VERTICAL_ONLY, zone input. The pivot latitude and longitude the
 1914:             # grid lookups need come from inverse-projecting through the

 1922:                 northing_m,
 1923:                 easting_m,
 1924:                 settings.source_zone,
 1925:                 settings.source_zone,
 1926:                 context,
 1927:             )
 1928:             output_northing = row.northing
 1929:             output_easting = row.easting
 1930:         else:
 1931:             conversion = convert_point(
 1932:                 northing_m,
 1933:                 easting_m,
 1934:                 settings.source_zone,
 1935:                 settings.target_zone,
 1936:                 context,
 1937:             )
 1938:             output_northing = settings.output_unit.from_meters(
 1939:                 conversion.target_northing
 1940:             )
 1941:             output_easting = settings.output_unit.from_meters(conversion.target_easting)
 1942: 
 1943:     # Elevation is orthometric height: it does not change with the horizontal
 1944:     # zone. Only its unit changes - and it changes in EVERY direction,
 1945:     # including State Plane to geodetic.
 1946:     #
 1947:     # That last clause used to be an exception: the elevation was left in the
 1948:     # input unit when the horizontal columns became degrees, on the reasoning
 1949:     # that a geodetic export has no linear unit. It does: the Z column. Three
 1950:     # separate surfaces already said so - this class's own docstring, the audit
 1951:     # CSV's "in <in>, out <out>" label, and the job record's "Units out" line -
 1952:     # while the clean export wrote feet. A reader who re-imported the file as
 1953:     # the record instructs computed the elevation factor at 900 m instead of
 1954:     # 274.3 m, a 98 ppm error, and read a Z field 625.680 m from the truth.
 1955:     # The unit now follows the output unit end to end (WP-R2 fix A).
 1956:     elevation_m = (
 1957:         settings.input_unit.to_meters(row.elevation)
 1958:         if row.elevation is not None
 1959:         else None
 1960:     )
 1961: 
 1962:     # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 1963:     # Ellipsoid height in, orthometric height out - H = h - N (the owner's
 1964:     # feature, 2026-08-11).
 1965:     #
 1966:     # ``supplied_m`` keeps the height exactly as the file gave it, because
 1967:     # HORIZONTAL MODE WRITES THAT NUMBER BACK UNCHANGED (the owner's
 1968:     # instruction: "in horizontal only mode, the elevations should be passed
 1969:     # through unchanged, regardless of the input"). Everything else works from
 1970:     # ``elevation_m``, and the point of rebinding it HERE, before anything
 1971:     # reads it, is the invariant that establishes:
 1972:     #
 1973:     #     from this line down, elevation_m is an ORTHOMETRIC height in metres,
 1974:     #     on every path, in every mode.
 1975:     #
 1976:     # That invariant is why the eight places below need no edit at all.
 1977:     # Assigning only ``height_m`` instead would have been silently overwritten
 1978:     # a few lines later by the identity branch's ``apply_shift(elevation_m,
 1979:     # ...)`` - on the flagship same-datum job the feature would have done
 1980:     # nothing at all - and would have fed a raw ellipsoid height to VERTCON and
 1981:     # to #41's source-era factor path. Found by the design review before the
 1982:     # code was written; pinned by
 1983:     # ``test_the_identity_branch_cannot_overwrite_the_converted_height``.
 1984:     #
 1985:     # ``grid`` is the right grid to read: with the swap refused for ellipsoid
 1986:     # input (``run``), the h -> H model IS ``factors_geoid_model`` in every
 1987:     # accepted configuration, and ``grid`` is loaded from exactly that record.
 1988:     # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 1989:     supplied_m = elevation_m
 1990:     ellipsoid_reading: EllipsoidHeightReading | None = None
 1991:     if settings.input_height_kind is HeightKind.ELLIPSOID and elevation_m is not None:
 1992:         model = factors_geoid_model(settings, transformation)
 1993:         if grid is None or model is None:
 1994:             raise ValueError(
 1995:                 f"{context}: the input heights are stated as ellipsoid heights "
 1996:                 f"but this job carries no geoid model, so no geoid separation "

 1999:                 f"wiring defect."
 2000:             )
 2001:         try:
 2002:             separation_m = geoid.geoid_height(
 2003:                 conversion.latitude, conversion.longitude, grid
 2004:             )
 2005:         except geoid.GeoidError as error:
 2006:             # No separation, so no orthometric height. In the vertical modes
 2007:             # that refuses the Z outright - those modes exist to produce a

 2014:             warnings.append(
 2015:                 ConversionWarning(
 2016:                     code=(

 2018:                         if settings.vertical_mode.converts_elevations
 2019:                         else WarningCode.GEOID_UNAVAILABLE
 2020:                     ),
 2021:                     message=(
 2022:                         f"{context}: the height {row.elevation:,.3f} "
 2023:                         f"{settings.input_unit.code} was supplied as an "
 2024:                         f"ELLIPSOID height, but no {model.name} geoid height "
 2025:                         f"is available at {conversion.latitude:.6f}, "
 2026:                         f"{conversion.longitude:.6f}, so the orthometric "
 2027:                         f"height H = h - N could not be computed for it. "
 2028:                         + (
 2029:                             "No elevation is written for this point and its "
 2030:                             "elevation and combined factors read "
 2031:                             if settings.vertical_mode.converts_elevations
 2032:                             else "The Z column carries the ellipsoid height "
 2033:                             "as supplied, unconverted, and the elevation and "
 2034:                             "combined factors read "
 2035:                         )
 2036:                         + f"{formatting.NOT_AVAILABLE}. The HORIZONTAL "
 2037:                         f"coordinate is unaffected and stands: it does not "

 2039:                         f"{error}"
 2040:                     ),
 2041:                 )
 2042:             )
 2043:         else:
 2044:             orthometric_m = elevation_m - separation_m

 2048:                 ellipsoid_height_m=elevation_m,
 2049:                 geoid_height_m=separation_m,
 2050:                 orthometric_height_m=orthometric_m,
 2051:             )
 2052:             elevation_m = orthometric_m
 2053: 
 2054:     # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 2055:     # Vertical shift - plan section 3.6 step 3, and it MUST run before the
 2056:     # geoid lookup and the factors below, because GEOID18/GEOID12B N and the
 2057:     # elevation factor are defined against the TARGET-era (NAVD 88) height.
 2058:     # The ordering's effect on the elevation factor is ~0.02 ppm - negligible,
 2059:     # and nobody should mistake the factor for the reason. The reason is the
 2060:     # Z VALUE ITSELF: an unshifted height is out by ~0.46 ft across Michigan
 2061:     # (plan section 3.6).
 2062:     #
 2063:     # ``height_m`` is the height everything downstream uses - the geoid gate,
 2064:     # the factors, and the Z column. For a horizontal job it IS elevation_m,
 2065:     # untouched, so that path is byte-identical to what shipped.
 2320:     # The Z that gets WRITTEN, and the one line where the mode decides
 2321:     # anything about it. Horizontal mode passes the supplied height through
 2322:     # untouched - the owner's instruction - so a GNSS file converted in
 2323:     # horizontal mode keeps its ellipsoid heights in the Z column and gains
 2324:     # only correct factors. The vertical modes write the orthometric height,
 2325:     # shifted. With ORTHOMETRIC input the two are the same value and every
 2326:     # pre-existing job is byte-identical.
 2327:     written_m = height_m if settings.vertical_mode.converts_elevations else supplied_m
 2328:     output_elevation = (
 2329:         settings.output_unit.from_meters(written_m)
 2330:         if written_m is not None
 2331:         else None
 2332:     )
 2333: 
 2334:     # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 2335:     # The height the FACTORS use - era consistency (DESIGN.md #41, superseding
 2336:     # plan section 3.5's target-datum-only rule). The geoid separation N is
 2337:     # defined against the geoid model's own vertical datum (NAVD 88 for both
 2338:     # shipped models), so h = H + N is honest only when H is in that same
 2339:     # datum. For an NGVD29 -> NAVD88 job that is the SHIFTED height, which is
 2340:     # why the shift precedes the factors; for a NAVD88 -> NGVD29 job it is the
 2341:     # SOURCE height - using the shifted NGVD 29 height there would mix the
 2342:     # eras by exactly the shift (~0.02 ppm in the factor; small, but wrong in
 2343:     # a number this program prints to its last digit). A job whose geoid
 2344:     # model matches NEITHER endpoint datum was refused before any point
 2345:     # converted (_require_vertical_settings). A coverage-refused point keeps
 2346:     # factor_height_m None deliberately: its factors read N/A with the
 2347:     # warning, era-splitting a half-failed point would be cleverness in an
 2348:     # audit trail.
 2349:     # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 2350:     factor_height_m = height_m
 2351:     if (
 2352:         vertical_reading is not None
 2353:         and height_m is not None
 2354:         and factors_use_source_era(settings, vertical_reading.transformation)
 2355:     ):
 2356:         factor_height_m = elevation_m
 2357: 
 2358:     geoid_height = None
 2359:     if grid is not None and factor_height_m is not None:
 2360:         # The model `grid` was loaded from, named the same way `run` chose it,
 2361:         # so the warning below cannot name a model this point did not consult.
 2362:         # Non-None whenever `grid` is: `run` derives one from the other.
 2363:         factors_model = factors_geoid_model(settings, transformation)
 2364:         geoid_model_consulted = (
 2365:             factors_model.name if factors_model is not None else "geoid"
 2366:         )
 2367:         try:
 2368:             geoid_height = geoid.geoid_height(
 2369:                 conversion.latitude, conversion.longitude, grid
 2370:             )
 2371:         except geoid.GeoidError as error:
 2372:             # Outside the shipped tile. The horizontal conversion is unaffected
 2373:             # and stands; only the elevation-dependent factors are unavailable,
 2374:             # and factors_at reports that as None rather than inventing one.
 2375:             #
 2376:             # It must also be SAID. Setting geoid_height to None on its own is
 2377:             # indistinguishable downstream from a point that carried no
 2378:             # elevation at all: the same two factor columns read N/A, and the
 2379:             # job record's ELEVATIONS section then listed this point under
 2380:             # "blank elevation field" - a falsehood about a point whose Z was
 2381:             # recorded. The warning carries the distinction to the audit CSV,
 2382:             # to the report's WARNINGS section, and to the screen (WP-R2 fix C).
 2383:             geoid_height = None
 2384:             warnings.append(
 2385:                 ConversionWarning(
 2386:                     code=WarningCode.GEOID_UNAVAILABLE,
 2387:                     message=(
 2388:                         f"{context}: the elevation "
 2389:                         # Not "read from the file": a typed point has none.
 2390:                         f"{row.elevation:,.3f} {settings.input_unit.code} was "
 2391:                         # The model this job actually consulted - the FACTORS
 2392:                         # side, which is the side `grid` was loaded from. It
 2393:                         # was `settings.geoid_model` until per-side selection
 2394:                         # (DESIGN.md #50) made that a different question: on a
 2395:                         # NAVD 88 -> NGVD 29 job the output side has no model
 2396:                         # at all (NGVD 29 has none), the factors run off the
 2397:                         # INPUT side, and naming settings.geoid_model here
 2398:                         # raised AttributeError on None instead of warning.
 2399:                         f"supplied, but no {geoid_model_consulted} "
 2400:                         f"geoid height is available at "
 2401:                         f"{conversion.latitude:.6f}, {conversion.longitude:.6f}, "
 2402:                         f"so the elevation factor and combined factor for this "
 2403:                         f"point are {formatting.NOT_AVAILABLE} rather than a "
 2404:                         f"number. The HORIZONTAL "
 2405:                         f"coordinate is unaffected and stands: it does not "
 2406:                         f"depend on elevation at all. Underlying reason: "
 2407:                         f"{error}"
 2408:                     ),
 2409:                 )
 2410:             )
 2411: 
 2412:     # The height in the geoid model's own era - plan section 3.6 step 5 as
 2413:     # amended by #41. For a horizontal job factor_height_m is elevation_m
 2414:     # untouched, so nothing changes.
 2415:     factors = factors_at(
 2416:         conversion.target_scale_factor, factor_height_m, geoid_height
 2417:     )
 2418: 
 2419:     return ConvertedPoint(
 2420:         row=row,
 2421:         conversion=conversion,
 2422:         factors=factors,
 2423:         output_northing=output_northing,
 2424:         output_easting=output_easting,
 2425:         output_elevation=output_elevation,
 2426:         vertical=vertical_reading,
 2427:         ellipsoid_height=ellipsoid_reading,
 2428:         geoid_swap=geoid_swap_reading,
 2429:         warnings=tuple(warnings) + conversion.warnings,
 2430:     )

  654: def test_the_frame_refusal_check_fails_when_the_registry_refusal_is_gone(
  655:     monkeypatch,
  656: ):
  657:     """Seeded with the defect it exists for: a bundle that ACCEPTS the crossing.
  658: 
  659:     ``frames.require_frame_path`` is replaced with one that hands back an
  660:     identity for any pair - which is precisely what a lost registry entry, or a
  661:     future edit that registered the bridge before it was verified, would look
  662:     like from inside the bundle. The check must refuse, and name both frames.
  663: 
  664:     **``convert`` is imported first, deliberately.** It binds
  665:     ``require_frame_path`` at ITS import, so whether this patch reaches the
  666:     public path depends on whether ``michspc.spc.convert`` was already imported
  667:     when the patch was applied - which depends on which tests ran before. That
  668:     is a test whose meaning changes with collection order; importing it here
  669:     fixes the binding, so this test seeds the REGISTRY call and only that.
  670:     """
  671:     from michspc.spc import convert, frames
  672: 
  673:     assert convert.require_frame_path is frames.require_frame_path
  674:     monkeypatch.setattr(
  675:         frames,
  676:         "require_frame_path",
  677:         lambda source, target: "a transformation that does not exist",
  678:     )

  681:         selftest.check_frame_refusal()

  684:     assert "NAD83(2011)" in message

  688: def test_the_frame_refusal_check_fails_on_the_wrong_exception_class(monkeypatch):
  689:     """The class is load-bearing, not only the fact that something was raised.
  690: 
  691:     ``michspc.job`` and the GUI both catch ``FrameMismatchError`` by name, so a
  692:     refusal raised as some other exception reaches the surveyor as a crash
  693:     rather than as an explanation - the shape of the WP-V2 dialect finding

  695:

  699:     the other's ``except`` clause unexercised - and which one gets seeded was,

   86: # The two halves of that same pattern as they appear once csv has split an
   87: # UNQUOTED grouped number into separate fields.
   88: _LEADING_GROUP = re.compile(r"^[+-]?\d{1,3}$")
   89: _FOLLOWING_GROUP = re.compile(r"^\d{3}(?:\.\d+)?$")
   90: 
   91: # U+FEFF, the byte order mark, written as an escape rather than as the character
   92: # itself: docs/DESIGN.md amendment #7 records what an invisible mark in a source
   93: # file costs, and a literal one here would be exactly that.
   94: _BYTE_ORDER_MARK = "\ufeff"
   95: 
   96: # A bare number, used only to test whether the description begins with one.
   97: # Deliberately does not admit "nan" or "inf": those are refused as coordinates,
   98: # and a description that literally reads "nan" is text, not a shifted number.
   99: _NUMERIC_TOKEN = re.compile(r"^[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)$")
  100: 
  101: # An angle written as degrees, minutes and seconds, in the spellings a data
  102: # collector or a spreadsheet actually produces:
  103: #
  104: #     43Â°47'59.8"N     43 47 59.8 N     43-47-59.8     43d47m59.8s     43:47:59.8N
  105: #
  106: # This reader takes DECIMAL DEGREES only (docs/DESIGN.md amendment #28), and
  107: # every one of those is refused by float() anyway. The pattern exists solely so
  108: # the refusal can say WHY rather than "not a number" - a surveyor whose export
  109: # wrote DMS needs to be told the format is wrong, not that his data is
  110: # unreadable. It is a diagnostic, never a parse: nothing downstream branches on
  111: # it, and a false positive costs a slightly wrong sentence in a message that
  112: # was going to be a refusal either way.
  113: _LOOKS_LIKE_DMS = re.compile(
  114:     r"""^[+-]?\d{1,3}          # degrees
  115:         \s*(?:[Â°Âºd:\-\s])\s*   # a separator of some kind
  116:         \d{1,2}                # minutes
  117:         \s*(?:['â€²m:\-\s]\s*\d{1,2}(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:["â€³s])?)?   # optional seconds
  118:         \s*[NSEWnsew]?$        # optional hemisphere letter
  119:     """,
  120:     re.VERBOSE,
  121: )

  124: class PnezdError(Exception):
  125:     """A coordinate file could not be read.
  126: 
  127:     Always names the file, the line number and the offending text, because a
  128:     refusal that does not say which row is wrong is not much use against a file
  129:     of several thousand points.

  149:     than flattening both into "missing".

  157: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  158: class PnezdFile:
  159:     """A parsed coordinate file."""
  160: 
  161:     path: Path
  162:     rows: tuple[PnezdRow, ...]
  163:     skipped_blank_lines: int
  164: 
  165:     sha256: str | None = None
  166:     """SHA-256 of the bytes these rows were parsed from, or None.
  167: 
  168:     Carried by the reader rather than recomputed later, because a digest taken
  169:     from the path afterwards certifies whatever is at that path *then* - not
  170:     what was converted. The reader reads the file once and hashes exactly the
  171:     bytes it decoded, so the two cannot be different bytes (WP-R3 fix 2).
  172: 
  173:     ``None`` is a statement, not an absence: "these rows did not come from bytes
  174:     this program read". ``parse_lines`` is handed already-decoded text and so
  175:     says None, and every surface that reports the digest must say so plainly
  176:     rather than substituting a hash of something else.
  177:     """
  178: 
  179:     @property
  180:     def points_without_elevation(self) -> tuple[PnezdRow, ...]:
  181:         return tuple(row for row in self.rows if not row.has_elevation)
  182:

  184: def _parse_number(text: str, field: str, line_number: int, line: str, path) -> float:
  185:     cleaned = text.strip()
  340:         f"(write 780000.000, not 780,000.000), or put double quotes around "
  341:         f"each number that contains them (\"780,000.000\"). Both are then read "
  342:         f"exactly as written."
  343:     )
  344: 
  345: 
  346: def parse_lines(lines, path="<text>") -> PnezdFile:
  347:     """Parse PNEZD content from an iterable of lines.
  348: 
  349:     Separated from file reading so the parser can be tested exhaustively
  350:     without touching the filesystem.
  351:     """
  352:     rows: list[PnezdRow] = []
  353:     blank = 0
  354:     first_seen: dict[str, int] = {}
  355: 
  356:     for line_number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
  357:         if line_number == 1:
  358:             # A byte order mark belongs to the file, not to the first point.
  359:             # ``read`` decodes utf-8-sig and so never delivers one - but its
  360:             # cp1252 fallback does, and so does any caller handing this
  361:             # function text it decoded itself, and the mark then rides into
  362:             # point_id, so point "101" arrives with an invisible mark glued to its front
  363:             # and matches nothing
  364:             # on the way back (WP-R2 fix G). Stripped here, at the one entry
  365:             # point every route funnels through, rather than on one of them.
  366:             line = line.lstrip(_BYTE_ORDER_MARK)
  367: 
  368:         if not line.strip():
  369:             blank += 1
  370:             continue
  371: 
  372:         # csv handles quoted fields containing commas; anything past the fifth
  373:         # field is description text that contained unquoted commas, and is
  374:         # rejoined below.
  375:         #
  376:         # strict=True is load-bearing, not tidiness. csv's default leniency
  377:         # REPAIRS malformed quoting instead of reporting it: an unterminated
  378:         # '"UNTERMINATED' becomes UNTERMINATED, and '"A"junk' becomes Ajunk.
  379:         # The parsed text then no longer represents the file, with no refusal
  380:         # anywhere - which for a description field is a survey note silently
  381:         # rewritten (WP-R2 fix E). csv.Error is converted to this module's own
  382:         # refusal so it names the line and says what is wrong, like every other
  383:         # refusal here.
  384:         try:
  385:             fields = next(csv.reader(io.StringIO(line), strict=True))
  386:         except csv.Error as error:
  387:             raise PnezdError(
  388:                 f"{path}, line {line_number}: the double quotes on this row are "
  389:                 f"malformed, so it is refused rather than repaired.\n"
  390:                 f"  {line.strip()!r}\n"
  391:                 f"The CSV reader reported: {error}.\n"
  392:                 f"A quoted field must open and close with a double quote and "
  393:                 f"must be followed by a comma or the end of the line - "
  394:                 f'101,1,2,3,"IRON PIPE, BENT". A double quote INSIDE a quoted '
  395:                 f'field is written twice - "6"" PIPE". Repairing this row '
  396:                 f"instead would change the text the file actually holds."
  397:             ) from error
  398: 
  399:         if len(fields) < 4:
  400:             raise PnezdError(
  401:                 f"{path}, line {line_number}: found {len(fields)} field(s), "
  402:                 f"need at least 4.\n  {line.strip()!r}\n"
  403:                 f"Expected: point, northing, easting, elevation, description - "
  404:                 f"with no header row. If this file has a header, remove it."
  405:             )
  406: 
  407:         point_id = fields[0].strip()
  408:         if not point_id:
  409:             raise PnezdError(
  410:                 f"{path}, line {line_number}: the point identifier is blank.\n"
  411:                 f"  {line.strip()!r}\n"
  412:                 f"Every point must be identifiable, or the converted file "
  413:                 f"cannot be matched back to this one."
  414:             )
  415: 
  416:         # Two rows claiming the same identifier is refused, not resolved. Both
  417:         # would parse, both would be converted, and both would be written into
  418:         # the export as point 101 - after which the job record names points by
  419:         # an identifier that no longer picks out one of them, and a CAD import
  420:         # either overwrites the first with the second or stops. Neither outcome
  421:         # can be corrected from the export, because the export no longer says
  422:         # which row was which.
  423:         #
  424:         # The owner's decision, and DESIGN.md section 7's rule that loaders
  425:         # validate as strictly as the UI. Compared exactly, after stripping
  426:         # surrounding whitespace: "101" and "101 " are the same point written
  427:         # untidily, but "CP4" and "cp4" are two identifiers this program has no
  428:         # authority to declare the same, and folding case would refuse a file
  429:         # that is legitimate (WP-R2 fix D).
  430:         if point_id in first_seen:
  431:             raise PnezdError(
  432:                 f"{path}, line {line_number}: the point identifier "
  433:                 f"{point_id!r} is already used on line {first_seen[point_id]}, "
  434:                 f"so this file is refused rather than converted.\n"
  435:                 f"  {line.strip()!r}\n"
  436:                 f"Two rows sharing one identifier both convert and both are "
  437:                 f"written out as point {point_id!r}. The job record then names "
  438:                 f"a point that could be either of them, and importing the "
  439:                 f"result into CAD either overwrites the first with the second "
  440:                 f"or fails outright - and nothing in the export says which row "
  441:                 f"was which. Give the duplicate a distinct identifier, or "
  442:                 f"delete whichever row is the stale one, and convert again."
  443:             )
  444:         first_seen[point_id] = line_number
  445: 
  446:         description = ",".join(fields[4:]).strip() if len(fields) > 4 else ""
  447: 
  448:         # Before any field is read as a number, because the literal reading of
  449:         # an ambiguous row parses perfectly well - that is the whole problem.
  450:         _refuse_ambiguous_grouping(fields, description, line_number, line, path)
  451: 
  452:         northing = _parse_number(fields[1], "northing", line_number, line, path)
  453:         easting = _parse_number(fields[2], "easting", line_number, line, path)
  454:         elevation, was_zero = _parse_elevation(fields[3], line_number, line, path)
  455: 
  456:         rows.append(
  457:             PnezdRow(
  458:                 line_number=line_number,
  459:                 point_id=point_id,
  460:                 northing=northing,
  461:                 easting=easting,
  462:                 elevation=elevation,
  463:                 description=description,
  464:                 elevation_was_zero=was_zero,
  465:             )
  466:         )
  467: 
  468:     if not rows:
  469:         raise PnezdError(
  470:             f"{path} contains no coordinate rows. An empty file is refused "
  471:             f"rather than producing an empty export that would look like a "
  472:             f"successful conversion."
  473:         )
  474: 
  475:     return PnezdFile(path=Path(path), rows=tuple(rows), skipped_blank_lines=blank)

  411:         target_convergence=convergence,
  412:         target_scale_factor=scale,
  413:         warnings=warnings,
  414:     )
  415: 
  416: 
  417: def geodetic_position(
  418:     latitude: float,
  419:     longitude: float,
  420:     source_frame: ReferenceFrame,
  421:     context: str = "point",
  422: ) -> PointConversion:
  423:     """A geodetic position with no zone on either end.
  424: 
  425:     Exists for the vertical-only job whose input is geodetic
  426:     (``michspc.job``, ``Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY`` with ``source_zone=None``):
  427:     the vertical shift and the geoid lookup need the pivot latitude and
  428:     longitude, and nothing in that job involves a State Plane zone. Every
  429:     zone-derived field is None - never a fabricated zone, whose scale factor
  430:     and convergence would be plausible numbers describing a projection nobody
  431:     chose. ``factors_at`` accepts the None scale factor and reports the grid
  432:     scale and combined factors as absent while still computing the elevation
  433:     factor, which needs no zone.
  434: 
  435:     ``source_frame`` is required with no default, exactly as
  436:     ``project_point`` requires it and for the same reason: a latitude and
  437:     longitude alone do not say which frame they belong to, and the NGS grids
  438:     this position is looked up in are published against NAD 83. No projection
  439:     runs here, so no extent warning can be raised - there is no zone to have
  440:     an extent.
  441:     """
  442:     if not isinstance(source_frame, ReferenceFrame):
  443:         raise TypeError(
  444:             f"geodetic_position needs the reference frame the position is "
  445:             f"expressed in, as its third argument; got "
  446:             f"{type(source_frame).__name__} ({source_frame!r}). A latitude "
  447:             f"and longitude do not carry their own frame. Pass "
  448:             f"michspc.spc.frames.NAD83_2011 for an NAD 83 position."
  449:         )
  450: 
  451:     return PointConversion(
  452:         source_zone=None,
  453:         target_zone=None,
  454:         frame=source_frame,
  455:         source_northing=None,
  456:         source_easting=None,
  457:         latitude=latitude,
  458:         longitude=longitude,
  459:         target_northing=None,
  460:         target_easting=None,
  461:         source_convergence=None,
  462:         source_scale_factor=None,
  463:         target_convergence=None,
  464:         target_scale_factor=None,
  465:         warnings=(),
  466:     )
  255: # NAD83(2011) <-> NATRF2022 bridge is deferred with its evidence recorded in
  256: # docs/DEFERRED-NATRF2022-BRIDGE.md, and it is deferred because NGS has not
  257: # published the transformation, not because it was not attempted.
  258: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  259: 
  260: _IDENTITY_CITATION = (
  261:     "Source and target frame are the same, so no transformation is applied and "
  262:     "the position is reported in the frame it was supplied in. No published "
  263:     "product is involved and none is needed."
  264: )
  265: 
  266: 
  267: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  268: class FrameTransformation:
  269:     """One published way to move a position from one reference frame to another.
  270: 
  271:     An identity record - source and target the same frame - carries no
  272:     parameters at all, and today every record in the registry is one. Identity
  273:     is an explicit record rather than a ``source is target`` shortcut in the
  274:     caller, because a NAD83(2011) to NAD83(2011) job is legitimate and the
  275:     outputs must be able to STATE "both frames NAD83(2011), no transformation
  276:     applied" rather than have that fall out of an untested branch. That is the
  277:     contract ``VerticalTransformation``'s identity records already hold.
  278: 
  279:     **The parameterized fields are deliberately absent, not defaulted to
  280:     nothing.** When the bridge lands they arrive as optional fields defaulting
  281:     to ``None`` and these records construct unchanged; a half-specified record
  282:     is then caught the way ``VerticalTransformation.__post_init__`` catches one.
  283:     Until then ``__post_init__`` below refuses any record that is not an
  284:     identity, so this module cannot grow a silent pass-through between two
  285:     different frames - which is the exact shape of the error it exists to
  286:     prevent.
  287:     """
  288: 
  289:     source: ReferenceFrame
  290:     target: ReferenceFrame
  291:     citation: str
  292: 
  293:     def __post_init__(self) -> None:
  294:         # if/raise, never assert: the suite and the shipped program both run
  295:         # under -O, which strips asserts (DESIGN.md section 7).
  296:         if self.source.code != self.target.code:
  297:             raise ValueError(
  298:                 f"Frame transformation {self.source.code} -> "
  299:                 f"{self.target.code} carries no parameters, which would leave "
  300:                 f"the position unchanged while relabelling its frame. "
  301:                 f"NAD83(2011) and NATRF2022 differ by one to two metres, so "
  302:                 f"that is a boundary-moving error that looks entirely "
  303:                 f"ordinary. Only a frame with itself may be an identity, and "
  304:                 f"an identity is all this registry carries today "
  305:                 f"(docs/DEFERRED-NATRF2022-BRIDGE.md, DESIGN.md #62)."
  306:             )
  307: 
  308:         if not self.citation.strip():
  309:             raise ValueError(
  310:                 f"Frame transformation {self.source.code} -> "
  311:                 f"{self.target.code} has an empty citation. Every record must "
  312:                 f"be able to say what it does to a position and on whose "
  313:                 f"authority; outputs quote these."
  314:             )
  315: 
  316:     @property
  317:     def is_identity(self) -> bool:
  318:         """True when no transformation is applied and the position is unchanged.
  319: 
  320:         Derived from the record's own frames rather than stored, so it cannot
  321:         drift from what ``__post_init__`` checked. Every record answers True
  322:         today; the property is written so that it keeps answering correctly
  323:         when parameterized records join it.
  324:         """
  325:         return self.source.code == self.target.code
  326: 
  327:     @property
  328:     def direction_statement(self) -> str:
  329:         """The transformation in words. What outputs quote.
  330: 
  331:         Written from the record's own fields for the reason
  332:         ``VerticalTransformation.direction_statement`` is: a record and the
  333:         sentence describing it must be incapable of disagreeing.
  334:         """
  335:         if self.is_identity:
  336:             return (
  337:                 f"Both positions are in {self.source.name} "
  338:                 f"({self.source.code}); no frame transformation is applied."
  339:             )
  340:         # Unreachable while the registry carries identities only - and it is
  341:         # written as a refusal rather than a guess so that a parameterized
  342:         # record added without its own sentence fails loudly here instead of
  343:         # printing a blank or a lie into a job record.
  344:         raise NotImplementedError(
  345:             f"Frame transformation {self.source.code} -> {self.target.code} "
  346:             f"is not an identity, so it must state its own arithmetic. Add "
  347:             f"that statement with the parameters "
  348:             f"(docs/DEFERRED-NATRF2022-BRIDGE.md)."
  349:         )
  350: 
  351:     def __str__(self) -> str:
  352:         return f"{self.source.code} -> {self.target.code}"
  353: 
  354: 
  355: _IDENTITY_NAD83_2011 = FrameTransformation(
  356:     source=NAD83_2011,
  357:     target=NAD83_2011,
  358:     citation=_IDENTITY_CITATION,
  359: )
  360: 
  361: _IDENTITY_NATRF2022 = FrameTransformation(
  362:     source=NATRF2022,
  363:     target=NATRF2022,
  364:     citation=_IDENTITY_CITATION,
  365: )

  368: # registered path of any kind, so that removing the usability check could never
  369: # leave a WGS 84 job quietly running as an identity - it would still have to
  370: # get past a missing registry entry. Pinned.
