  441: def _canonical(frame: ReferenceFrame) -> ReferenceFrame:
  442:     """The registry's own record for this frame's code, when it has one.
  443: 
  444:     A record rebuilt from a saved job, or hand-built by a caller, must not be
  445:     able to claim a status this module did not grant it - that is how an
  446:     unusable frame would slip through, and a hand-built ``ReferenceFrame`` is
  447:     a two-line thing to write. An unrecognised code is returned unchanged, so
  448:     it reaches the pair refusal below, which names it.
  449:     """
  450:     return _FRAMES_BY_CODE.get(frame.code, frame)
  451: 
  452: 
  453: def require_frame_path(
  454:     source: ReferenceFrame, target: ReferenceFrame
  455: ) -> FrameTransformation:
  456:     """The registered path for this pair of frames, or a loud refusal.
  457: 
  458:     Called on every conversion, and it replaces ``require_same_frame``: one
  459:     gate per path, returning the record that describes what was done, rather
  460:     than a check that returns nothing and a separate lookup that could
  461:     disagree with it.
  462: 
  463:     Within one frame the zone-to-zone conversion is an exact, reversible
  464:     re-projection of the same physical position, and this function returns
  465:     that frame's identity record.
  466: 
  467:     Two distinct refusals, because they mean different things to a user:
  468: 
  469:     * ``FrameNotUsableError`` - the frame is declared here but this program
  470:       cannot carry coordinates in it (WGS 84 today). Checked FIRST, so the
  471:       message names the frame rather than reporting a missing transformation
  472:       and implying one might be coming.
  473:     * ``FrameTransformationUnavailableError`` - both frames are usable, but no
  474:       transformation between them is published or implemented (NAD83(2011) to
  475:       NATRF2022 today, DESIGN.md #62).
  476: 
  477:     Never a silent pass-through. An untransformed position labelled as
  478:     transformed is a boundary-relevant error that looks entirely ordinary.
  479: 
  480:     Refuses a non-``ReferenceFrame`` argument by name, for the reason
  481:     docs/DESIGN.md amendment #11 finding 1 records: this program's core records
  482:     all carry ``code``, ``name`` and ``citation``, so a ``Zone``, a
  483:     ``VerticalDatum`` and a ``LinearUnit`` all duck-type through ``_canonical``
  484:     and would only fail several lines later on ``is_usable`` - as an
  485:     ``AttributeError``, which walks straight through the
  486:     ``except FrameMismatchError`` every caller of this module writes. Passing
  487:     ``source_zone`` where ``source_zone.frame`` was meant is the likeliest
  488:     version of that mistake, and it is one character.
  489:     """
  490:     for label, frame in (("source", source), ("target", target)):
  491:         if not isinstance(frame, ReferenceFrame):
  492:             raise TypeError(
  493:                 f"require_frame_path needs a michspc.spc.frames."
  494:                 f"ReferenceFrame as its {label}; got "
  495:                 f"{type(frame).__name__} ({frame!r}). Every record in this "
  496:                 f"core carries code, name and citation, so a zone, a vertical "
  497:                 f"datum or a unit reaches this function without complaint and "
  498:                 f"would be asked whether it is a usable reference FRAME. Pass "
  499:                 f"michspc.spc.frames.NAD83_2011, or a zone's own .frame."
  500:             )
  501: 
  502:     resolved_source = _canonical(source)
  503:     resolved_target = _canonical(target)
  504: 
  505:     unusable: list[ReferenceFrame] = []
  506:     for frame in (resolved_source, resolved_target):
  507:         if not frame.is_usable and frame.code not in {f.code for f in unusable}:
  508:             unusable.append(frame)
  509: 
  510:     if unusable:
  511:         offenders = " and ".join(f.code for f in unusable)
  512:         verb = "are" if len(unusable) > 1 else "is"
  513:         details = " ".join(f"{f.code} ({f.name}): {f.citation}." for f in unusable)
  514:         usable = ", ".join(f.code for f in ALL_FRAMES if f.is_usable)
  515:         raise FrameNotUsableError(
  516:             f"Cannot convert from {resolved_source.code} to "
  517:             f"{resolved_target.code}: {offenders} {verb} declared in this "
  518:             f"program but not usable. {details} Any coordinate this program "
  519:             f"reported in that frame would be invented rather than converted. "
  520:             f"The reference frames this program can carry today are: {usable}."
  521:         )
  522: 
  523:     try:
  524:         return _TRANSFORMATIONS_BY_CODE[(resolved_source.code, resolved_target.code)]
  525:     except KeyError:
  526:         known = ", ".join(f"{s} -> {t}" for s, t in sorted(_TRANSFORMATIONS_BY_CODE))
  527:         raise FrameTransformationUnavailableError(
  528:             f"Cannot convert from {resolved_source.code} to "
  529:             f"{resolved_target.code}: no transformation between these two "
  530:             f"reference frames is implemented. Registered paths are: {known}. "
  531:             f"Coordinates differ between NAD83(2011) and NATRF2022 by one to "
  532:             f"two metres - more than the width of a road, and nothing in the "
  533:             f"numbers shows it - so passing them through unchanged would "
  534:             f"silently corrupt them. NGS has not published the "
  535:             f"NAD83(2011) <-> NATRF2022 transformation: its own NCAT computes "

  144: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  145: class JobSettings:
  146:     """Everything the user chose. Recorded verbatim in the job record."""
  147: 
  148:     input_path: Path | None
  149:     """The file these coordinates were read from.
  150: 
  151:     **Required, with no default**, the idiom ``longitude_convention`` already
  152:     uses below. ``None`` is a statement, not an absence: "this job came from no
  153:     file". A single typed point says exactly that, and the alternative - a
  154:     fabricated placeholder path - is the plausible default docs/DESIGN.md
  155:     section 1 forbids, because it would put a file name that was never read into
  156:     the job record's INPUT block (amendment #26).
  157: 
  158:     Every read of this field is guarded, and each guard raises its own layer's
  159:     error rather than letting ``None`` travel: ``run`` needs it only when no
  160:     parsed source was handed in, and ``exports.output_stem`` and
  161:     ``report.build_report`` refuse without it.
  162:     """
  163: 
  164:     output_directory: Path | None
  165:     """The folder this job's archive is written into.
  166: 
  167:     **Required, with no default**, and ``None`` is again a statement: "this job
  168:     produces no file". The single-point path converts and displays, writing
  169:     nothing at all, so it has no folder to name and does not invent one.
  170:     ``run`` never reads this field; ``exports.archive_path`` and
  171:     ``report.build_report`` refuse without it (amendment #26).
  172:     """
  173: 
  174:     direction: Direction
  175: 
  176:     source_zone: Zone | None
  177:     target_zone: Zone | None

  180:     output_unit: LinearUnit
  181: 
  182:     longitude_convention: LongitudeConvention | None
  183:     """Which sign convention the file's longitudes use.
  184: 
  185:     **Required, with no default** (docs/DESIGN.md section 7). A default here is
  186:     the failure the rule exists to prevent: a geodetic input file written
  187:     positive west, converted as though it were negative west, lands 11,634,618 m
  188:     away carrying nothing louder than an outside-zone-extent warning. The field
  189:     is declared before the defaulted fields only because a frozen dataclass may
  190:     not put a field without a default after one that has one.
  191: 
  192:     ``None`` is a statement, not an absence: "this job never consults the
  193:     convention". Only a pure zone-to-zone job may say it - the grid coordinates
  194:     on both ends carry no longitude - and ``run`` refuses any other direction
  195:     that arrives with None rather than choosing one.
  196:     """
  197: 
  198:     geoid_model: geoid.GeoidModel | None = geoid.GEOID18_MODEL
  199:     """The geoid model whose separations this job's factors are computed from.
  200: 
  201:     Replaces ``apply_geoid: bool`` (WP-V5, docs/PLAN-vertical-datums.md section
  202:     3.5): a bool could say only that *some* geoid was applied, and the job
  203:     record then named the model from a module constant that a second model
  204:     made ambiguous. The record chosen here is the one the audit CSV and the
  205:     job record report, so the settings and the outputs cannot disagree about
  206:     which grid the factors came from.
  207: 
  208:     ``None`` is a statement, not an absence - "no geoid was applied to this
  209:     job" - the idiom ``input_path`` and ``output_directory`` already use. No
  210:     interface offers it (the owner's "no none", plan section 5); it is a
  211:     capability of the core, kept so report.py's "Geoid model not applied"
  212:     branch stays honest and tested rather than dead.
  213:     """
  214: 
  215:     geodetic_frame: ReferenceFrame = NAD83_2011
  216:     """The reference frame this job's GEODETIC end is expressed in.
  217:

from pathlib import Path

from michspc import job as jobmod
from michspc.fileio import geoid, pnezd
from michspc.job import Direction, JobSettings, LongitudeConvention, VerticalMode, run
from michspc.spc.frames import NAD83_2011, NATRF2022, WGS84
from michspc.spc.units import METERS
from michspc.spc.vertical import HeightKind, NAVD88, NGVD29
from michspc.spc.zones import zone_by_code

z22 = zone_by_code('261008')
statewide = zone_by_code('260001')
geo = pnezd.parse_lines(['1,43.0,-84.5,200.000,P\\n'], path='memory-geo.csv')
grid22 = pnezd.parse_lines(['1,251023.811677263118,1462701.575467889430,198.885,GNSS\\n'], path='memory-grid22.csv')
grid83 = pnezd.parse_lines(['1,100000.0,4000000.0,200.000,P\\n'], path='memory-grid83.csv')

def settings(direction, source_zone, target_zone, frame=NAD83_2011, *, ellipsoid=False, vertical=False):
    return JobSettings(
        input_path=Path('never-read.csv'), output_directory=None,
        direction=direction, source_zone=source_zone, target_zone=target_zone,
        input_unit=METERS, output_unit=METERS,
        longitude_convention=(
            LongitudeConvention.NEGATIVE_WEST
            if direction in (Direction.GEODETIC_TO_ZONE, Direction.ZONE_TO_GEODETIC)
            or (direction is Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY and source_zone is None)
            else None
        ),
        geodetic_frame=frame,
        vertical_mode=VerticalMode.VERTICAL if vertical else VerticalMode.HORIZONTAL,
        source_vertical_datum=NAVD88 if vertical else None,
        target_vertical_datum=NAVD88 if vertical else None,
        geoid_model=geoid.GEOID18_MODEL,
        input_height_kind=HeightKind.ELLIPSOID if ellipsoid else HeightKind.ORTHOMETRIC,
    )

def outcome(label, fn):
    try:
        value = fn()
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f'{label}: REFUSED {type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0]}')
    else:
        print(f'{label}: ACCEPTED {value}')

# Exact HIGH: prove settings refusal occurs without consulting the reader.
read_calls = 0
original_read = jobmod.pnezd.read
def forbidden_read(path):
    global read_calls
    read_calls += 1
    raise AssertionError('FILE READER WAS REACHED')
jobmod.pnezd.read = forbidden_read
try:
    exact = settings(Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY, z22, None, NATRF2022, ellipsoid=True, vertical=True)
    outcome('HIGH exact vertical-only 261008 h=198.885', lambda: run(exact))
finally:
    jobmod.pnezd.read = original_read
print(f'HIGH exact file-reader calls: {read_calls}')

# Every legitimate job shape whose input-height frame is NATRF2022.
natrf_shapes = [
    ('G2Z geodetic branch', settings(Direction.GEODETIC_TO_ZONE, None, z22, NATRF2022, ellipsoid=True), geo),
    ('Z2G zone-input branch', settings(Direction.ZONE_TO_GEODETIC, z22, None, NATRF2022, ellipsoid=True), grid22),
    ('Z2Z zone-input branch', settings(Direction.ZONE_TO_ZONE, z22, z22, NATRF2022, ellipsoid=True), grid22),
    ('VERTICAL zone-input branch', settings(Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY, z22, None, NATRF2022, ellipsoid=True, vertical=True), grid22),
    ('VERTICAL geodetic branch', settings(Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY, None, None, NATRF2022, ellipsoid=True, vertical=True), geo),
]
for label, cfg, src in natrf_shapes:
    outcome(label, lambda cfg=cfg, src=src: run(cfg, src).points[0].output_elevation)

cross = settings(Direction.ZONE_TO_ZONE, z83, z22, NAD83_2011, ellipsoid=True)
outcome('Z2Z NAD83 source to NATRF target ellipsoid', lambda: run(cross, grid83).points[0].output_elevation)

# Controls.

nad_source = pnezd.parse_lines(['1,44.2520,-85.4012,166.720,GNSS\\n'], path='memory-nad.csv')
outcome('CONTROL NAD83 ellipsoid h=166.720', lambda: f\"H={run(nad_ellipsoid, nad_source).points[0].output_elevation:.12f}\")
orth2022 = settings(Direction.GEODETIC_TO_ZONE, None, z22, NATRF2022)
ortho_source = pnezd.parse_lines(['101,42.8,-85.15,300.0,P\\n'], path='memory-ortho.csv')
outcome('CONTROL NATRF2022 orthometric H=300', lambda: (run(ortho2022, ortho_source).points[0].output_northing, run(ortho2022, ortho_source).points[0].factors.combined_factor))

vertical = settings(Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY, None, None, NAD83_2011, vertical=True)

stray_z2g = settings(Direction.ZONE_TO_GEODETIC, z22, statewide, NATRF2022)
stray_vertical = settings(Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY, z22, statewide, NATRF2022, vertical=True)

    ('STRAY G2Z source=260001 target=261008', stray_g2z, geo),

):

Two ways on: state that the Z column holds ORTHOMETRIC elevations - an elevation is a height above the geoid, not above a frame's ellipsoid, and every 2022 zone converts one today - or wait, as the cross-frame conversions do, for NGS to publish the transformation.

def cfg(direction, source_zone, target_zone, frame, ellipsoid=True, vertical=False):
    return JobSettings(
        input_path=Path('memory.csv'), output_directory=None,

        geodetic_frame=frame,
        vertical_mode=VerticalMode.VERTICAL if vertical else VerticalMode.HORIZONTAL,
        source_vertical_datum=NAVD88 if vertical else None,
        target_vertical_datum=NAVD88 if vertical else None,
        geoid_model=geoid.GEOID18_MODEL,
        input_height_kind=HeightKind.ELLIPSOID if ellipsoid else HeightKind.ORTHOMETRIC,
    )

import runpy
import pytest

ns = runpy.run_path('tests/test_selftest.py')
names = (
    'test_the_frame_refusal_check_fails_when_the_registry_refusal_is_gone',
    'test_the_frame_refusal_check_fails_on_the_wrong_exception_class',
)
for sequence in (names, tuple(reversed(names))):
    print('ORDER:', ' -> '.join(sequence))
    for name in sequence:
        patch = pytest.MonkeyPatch()
        try:
            ns[name](patch)
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f'  {name}: FAIL {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}')
        else:
            print(f'  {name}: PASS')
        finally:
            patch.undo()

from michspc.fileio import pnezd, report
from michspc.job import Direction, JobSettings, LongitudeConvention, VerticalMode, run
from michspc.spc.frames import NATRF2022
from michspc.spc.units import METERS
from michspc.spc.vertical import NAVD88, NGVD29
from michspc.spc.zones import zone_by_code

zsrc = zone_by_code('261008')
ztgt = zone_by_code('260001')
geo = pnezd.parse_lines(['1,43.0,-84.5,200.0,P\\n'], path='geo')
grid = pnezd.parse_lines(['1,251023.811677263118,1462701.575467889430,200.0,P\\n'], path='grid')
for direction in Direction:
    for has_source in (False, True):
        for has_target in (False, True):
            source_zone = zsrc if has_source else None
            target_zone = ztgt if has_target else None
            vertical = direction is Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY
            geodetic = direction in (Direction.GEODETIC_TO_ZONE, Direction.ZONE_TO_GEODETIC) or (vertical and source_zone is None)
            settings = JobSettings(
                input_path=Path('memory'), output_directory=None,
                direction=direction, source_zone=source_zone, target_zone=target_zone,
                input_unit=METERS, output_unit=METERS,
                longitude_convention=LongitudeConvention.NEGATIVE_WEST if geodetic else None,
                geodetic_frame=NATRF2022,
                vertical_mode=VerticalMode.VERTICAL if vertical else VerticalMode.HORIZONTAL,
                source_vertical_datum=NGVD29 if vertical else None,
                target_vertical_datum=NAVD88 if vertical else None,
            )
            source = geo if direction is Direction.GEODETIC_TO_ZONE or (vertical and source_zone is None) else grid
            label = f'{direction.name} source={has_source} target={has_target}'
            try:
                result = run(settings, source)
            except Exception as exc:
                print(f'{label}: REFUSED {type(exc).__name__}')
            else:
                record_zones = [z.code for z in report._job_zones(result.settings)]
                conversion = result.points[0].conversion
                actual = (
                    conversion.source_zone.code if conversion.source_zone else None,
                    conversion.target_zone.code if conversion.target_zone else None,
                )
                print(f'{label}: ACCEPTED record_zones={record_zones} conversion_zones={actual}')
